newsitem.title: USA: Moynihan probably will revise stadiums bill-aide.
newsitem.headline: Moynihan probably will revise stadiums bill-aide.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan, D-N.Y., probably will change the controversial effective date in a bill he introduced in June that would bar the use of tax-exempt bonds for stadium financings, a congressional aide said.
"When we reintroduce the bill in January, there is a good chance we will change the effective date," the aide said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
"We're not sure what the date is going to be, but it won't be June 14," the aide said.
The aide said, "If it gets changed, anything that's going on now will be exempted from it."
He said Moynihan is considering revising the effective date to when it is reintroduced, probably January 1997.
Moynihan had introduced the measure on June 14.
Following a chorus of criticism from bond groups, he announced June 28 that he would add transition language to protect projects that are far along in financing.
But he refused to drop the June 14 general effective date.
Then, Moynihan aides met with state and local government groups on July 11 to discuss the groups' concerns with the bill.
But, again, the aides did not pledge to revise the effective date, which municipal bond market spokesmen warn is disrupting the tax-exempt bond market.
The congressional aide stressed today that Moynihan's purpose in curbing tax exempt financing for stadiums is to "correct the law," not hurt municipalities.
"We're not trying to be bad guys here," he said.
